name: California

regulator.name: California Secretary of State, Special Filings Unit

law.name: Miller-Ayala Athlete Agents Act (Bus. & Prof. Code 18895 and following)

covers_nil_agents: Yes. Educ. Code 67456(c) says NIL agents must be licensed under this act (attorneys through the State Bar).
summary: File a disclosure statement with the Secretary of State ($30) and carry $100,000 in insurance or security.

steps.text: Fill out the Athlete Agent Disclosure Statement (SF-AA1)
steps.detail: Attach the schedule of fees you'll charge athletes.

steps.text: Get $100,000 in errors and omissions insurance or security
steps.detail: Insurance, a bond or cash deposit under Bus. & Prof. Code 18897.87.

steps.text: Mail it to the Secretary of State
steps.detail: Special Filings Unit, P.O. Box 942870, Sacramento, CA 94277-2870.

steps.text: Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Your pay and how it's figured, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: Put the WARNING TO STUDENT ATHLETE box next to their signature
Give the athlete a copy when they sign
Notify the athletic director within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, whichever comes first. The athlete may cancel within 15 days.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: Federal law (SPARTA) bans pre-dating or post-dating it.

steps.text: Report any change within 7 days on form SF-AA2

steps.detail: Names and addresses, contracts and recruiting costs.

steps.text: Never give gifts or money to recruit athletes or make false promises
steps.detail: This is a state and federal (SPARTA) rule.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: No renewal cycle is stated on the form. Confirm with the Secretary of State.
California's contract and school-notice rules (Bus. & Prof. Code 18897 and following) differ from the uniform act. The athlete has 15 days to cancel. Check the exact contract wording.
The contract and school-notice steps follow the uniform act's standard text. Check them against this state's statute before launch.
